name: Creamy Mushroom Pasta
steps: Check that the dry tagliatelle is eggless. Brush the mushrooms clean rather than soaking them, then slice evenly about 5 mm thick. Mince the garlic, strip the thyme leaves and chop the parsley. Keep the cream measured and ready, because the mushrooms brown quickly.

Bring 2300 ml water and 8 g salt to a rolling boil. Add the pasta, stir to separate and cook according to its packet until just al dente. Reserve 200 ml cloudy cooking water before draining. Do not rinse the pasta.

Meanwhile heat 20 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms in two batches so they can brown; leave each batch undisturbed for 2 minutes, then turn and cook about 4 minutes more until their water evaporates and edges deepen in colour. Return all mushrooms to the pan, add garlic and thyme, and stir for 45 seconds.

Lower heat to medium-low. Add the cream, remaining 10 g butter, 4 g salt and black pepper. Simmer gently for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until lightly thickened; do not boil hard or the cream may split. Add drained tagliatelle and 80 ml reserved pasta water. Toss for 1–2 minutes until a smooth sauce clings to the ribbons, adding more pasta water a spoonful at a time only if too thick.

Turn off the heat and fold in chopped parsley. Divide into four warm bowls and distribute the browned mushrooms evenly. Finish with a little more black pepper if desired and serve immediately while the sauce remains glossy.
tips: The reviewed photo shows ribbon pasta generously covered with visibly browned button mushrooms and a pale, clinging cream sauce flecked with thyme and parsley. Browning mushrooms before adding cream prevents a watery, grey sauce. No cheese is needed.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
